newsitem.title: FRANCE: Livret A account took 5 bln Fr in Q1 deposits -CDC.
newsitem.headline: Livret A account took 5 bln Fr in Q1 deposits -CDC.

text.p: French investors deposited five billion francs in Livret A tax-free, pass-book savings accounts in the first quarter of 1997 after withdrawing 75 billion last year, Philippe Lagayette, managing director of state bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) said on Tuesday.
"The situation is under control now. We had deposits of five billion francs during the first three months of 1997," Lagayette told a news conference.
A one percentage point cut in the interest rate on Livret A accounts to 3.5 percent prompted withdrawals totaling 75 billion francs in 1996, CDC said in its results statement.
Bond analysts have said the re-allocation of savings from Livret A into other savings vehicles was one of the factors helping to support the French government bond market in 1996.

CDC said the drain from Livret A accounts was offset by an increase in deposits into other savings vehicles, especially LEP (Livret d'epargne populaire) accounts which pay interest at 4.75 percent and had inflows of 56.7 billion francs during the year.
Overall, outstanding deposits in official savings vehicles climbed to 1,016 billion francs in 1996, up 53.4 bilion francs compared with 1995.
However CDC most of the increase was due to reinvestment of interest. New flows into savings accounts rose 19.8 billion francs, lower than the 47.8 billion franc increase in 1995.
CDC said this was partly linked to the drop in the saving ratio in France to 12.4 percent from 14.3 percent in 1995.
